stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one

Identify stripe orientation and index. If given seed lines run down-right (constant d = col - row), use d; if they run down-left (constant s = row + col), use s. Infer the period from the seed stripe offsets/residues and map each residue to its color, then color every cell accordingly. Demo evidence: a 15x15 input with stripes of colors 8,2,9 at s=4,11,15 produced color by s mod 3 (residues 1→8, 2→2, 0→9). A 5x5 input with stripes at sums 0 (6), 5 (1), 6 (6), 7 (2) produced f(s mod 4)=[6,1,6,2]. A 25x25 input with 7 stripe d=10 and 5 stripe d=-19 yielded checkerboard by diagonal parity. A 16x16 test had 2 stripe d=-15, 1 stripe d=-2, and 9 stripe d=14; these offsets mapped residues mod3 as 0→2, 1→1, 2→9, and filling via (col-row) mod3 solved it. Do not assume rotational symmetry from isolated tiny demo; these are periodic diagonal tiling tasks, using relevant diagonal coordinate and color-residue mapping.''')
